藏品名称_EN: Maki-e lacquerware with cloud and dragon pattern
描述_EN: A 16-petal flower-shaped daikago (food basket). The design includes a five-clawed dragon in the center of the lid's surface, bordered by a palace lantern and surrounded by four dragons, interspersed with cloud patterns, flames, and jewels. The petal-shaped interior on either side of the lid is decorated with cloud and dragon motifs, with clouds and bats at the joints, and with repeated lapidary and sumeru on either side of the vessel. These motifs were painted in black, vermilion, green and yellow lacquer, then carved with gold leaf to create the outlines and fill in, a technique known as zongxing. This technique is known as "zongxing". Zongxing flourished in China during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and was imported to Japan as a highly prized lacquerware product. Judging from its large, powerful shape and the form of the cloud and dragon motif, this piece is thought to have been made around the Wanli period (1573-1619).
描述_ZN: 一个16瓣的花形daikago（食品篮）。 设计包括盖子表面中央的五爪龙，边上有宫灯，周围有四条龙，中间穿插着云纹、火焰和珠宝。 盖子两侧的花瓣形内饰有云龙纹，接合处有云和蝙蝠，器身两侧反复有立波和须弥山。 这些图案是用黑色、朱色、绿色和黄色的漆画出来的，然后用金箔刻出轮廓并填满，这种技术被称为宗兴。 这种技术被称为 "宗兴"。 宗兴在中国明朝（1368-1644）时期非常兴盛，并作为一种非常珍贵的漆器产品被进口到日本。 从其巨大、有力的外形和云龙图案的形式来看，这件作品被认为是在万历年间（1573-1619）左右制作的。
